None of the four opens on the same construction and none is a question. An earlier draft titled 03 'Who at the inn owns the second booking?'; it was rejected under the operator_economy profile in content-os/rubric.md, which fails questions used as hooks. cross_short_check.hype_and_promise_audit: No hype-lexicon term, no income promise, no superlative about the channel, no figure in any title, no question used as a hook, no em dash and no emoji anywhere in the package.
cross_short_check.publish_order_reason: 01 first because it establishes in thirteen seconds the premise the other three assume, that commission recurs per booking, with no jargon and the fastest cold-viewer orientation. 04 second because its correction only lands once the viewer accepts that the charge repeats. 02 third because it is the most technical and the best mid-run piece for someone who already has the premise, and it is the strongest standalone unit if the run needs one to carry. 03 last because it resolves nothing, so it benefits most from the episode being live and from the other three having supplied its context, and it costs least if it underperforms.

reasons: No on-screen hook line in the first three seconds. The only element is a two-word relationship diagram, so a cold viewer gets no subject until speech arrives.
Sixteen seconds of three stacked questions with no resolved beat. Against the working-tree docs/content-rubric.md it hits the kill-list item 'no standalone narrow payoff'.
The end card repeats the question the speech just asked instead of advancing it.
The answer is one excluded word away. source-contract.json records W000584, 'Nobody', cut at 201.833s, so the fix is a one-beat extension and is a cut decision, not a copy decision.
